name: Computer Networks - IP Networking, Routing & TCP
description: IP addressing, subnetting, ARP, DHCP, fragmentation, ICMP, distance-vector & link-state routing, BGP, and TCP congestion control (CCN05-CCN07)

questions.question: Given IP 192.168.10.130/26, what is the network address?
How many usable host addresses are available in a /27 subnet?
Which of the following IP ranges is a private address range?
options: All of the above

questions.question: What is the broadcast address of the subnet 192.168.1.64/27?
Which statement about ARP cache entries is TRUE?
options: They are populated by DHCP and refreshed at lease renewal
They are dynamically learned and timed out after a period
They are distributed across the subnet via gratuitous ARP broadcasts
They are maintained by the default gateway on behalf of all hosts

questions.question: When a host sends an ARP request, which devices process it?
options: Only the router on the subnet
Only the destination host and the default gateway
All devices on the local broadcast domain
Only devices matching the target IP

questions.question: What is the subnet mask for a /22 network?
A host wants to reach 8.8.8.8, which is outside its subnet. Which MAC address will ARP resolve?
options: The MAC of 8.8.8.8 directly
The MAC of the local DNS resolver
The MAC of the default gateway
The MAC of the nearest ISP border router

questions.question: In IP fragmentation, which statement is TRUE about the More Fragments (MF) flag?
options: MF = 1 for the last fragment only
MF = 1 for all fragments including the last
MF = 1 for all fragments except the last
MF = 0 for all fragments

questions.question: If MTU = 1,000 bytes and IP header = 20 bytes, what is the maximum data payload per fragment (except the last)?
options: 960 bytes
972 bytes
976 bytes
980 bytes

questions.question: Which IP packet field is used to correctly reassemble fragmented IP packets at the destination?
options: TTL field
Protocol field
Identification field
Flags field

questions.question: Which situation will NOT generate an ICMP error message?
options: TTL reaches 0 at a router
Packet exceeds MTU with DF bit set
Packet sent to a broadcast or multicast address
Destination port unreachable

questions.question: A router receives a packet larger than the MTU with the DF (Don't Fragment) bit set to 1. What happens?
options: The router fragments the packet normally since the DF bit is advisory only
The router drops the packet and logs the event locally without notifying the source
The router drops the packet and sends an ICMP Type 3 Code 4 message to the source
The router buffers the packet and requests the source to reduce its MTU via TCP

questions.question: An ICMP error message includes which of the following?
options: The complete original packet up to the first 576 bytes
Only the original IP header without any payload
The original IP header plus the first 8 bytes of the original payload
The original IP header plus the full transport-layer segment

questions.question: When TTL becomes 0 at a router, what occurs?
options: The packet is forwarded to the next hop with TTL reset to its original value
The router sends a request to the source to retransmit with a higher TTL
The packet is dropped and an ICMP Time Exceeded message is sent to the source
The packet is queued until a route with fewer hops becomes available

questions.question: A DHCP Discover message is sent as:
options: Unicast to the known DHCP server
Broadcast to all devices on the network
Multicast to the DHCP group address
Anycast to the nearest DHCP server

questions.question: DHCP uses which UDP port numbers?
options: Port 53 (client), Port 67 (server)
Port 67 (client), Port 68 (server)
Port 68 (client), Port 67 (server)
Port 80 (client), Port 443 (server)

questions.question: What does a DHCP relay agent do?
options: Acts as a backup DHCP server and assigns addresses when the primary is unreachable
Caches recently issued DHCP leases to reduce server load on the local segment
Forwards client DHCP broadcasts as unicast to a DHCP server on another subnet
Translates DHCP lease information into DNS A records for the local zone

questions.question: A router is computing shortest paths from node D. The current tentative distances are: B = 11, C = 2. Which node will be added next to the confirmed set?
options: B (distance 11)
C (distance 2)
Both simultaneously
Neither until the full graph is known

questions.question: In a link-state routing system, a link between two routers fails. What is the correct system behavior?
options: Only the directly connected routers update their tables; others continue using stale routes
The network enters a count-to-infinity condition until hop limits are reached
A new link-state update is flooded to all routers, which then recompute paths
The failure is detected by BGP, which redistributes updated routes into the IGP

questions.question: A router receives a link-state packet from a neighbor. To which neighbors should it forward this packet?
options: To all neighbors including the sender, to ensure full coverage
To no neighbors; each router independently generates its own link-state packets
To all neighbors except the one it came from
Only to neighbors whose link costs are lower than the packet's advertised metric

questions.question: A router receives two identical link-state packets from the same source with the same sequence number. What should it do?
options: Process both to ensure the topology database remains consistent
Forward both copies to all neighbors to maximize reliability
Keep one and discard the duplicate
Send a retransmission request asking for a more recent update

questions.question: Why do link-state routing protocols avoid long-term routing loops?
options: They apply split horizon on all interfaces to suppress reverse routes
All routers compute consistent shortest-path trees from the same topology database
They reset all routing tables after each convergence cycle
Sequence numbers guarantee that no two routers choose different next hops

questions.question: Why does hierarchical routing reduce routing table size?
options: It applies prefix aggregation to compress multiple host routes into a single entry
It groups destinations into regions, requiring only regional-level entries for remote destinations
It replaces per-destination routes with a single default route to a central hub
It caches recently used routes and discards infrequently accessed entries

questions.question: A TCP connection has cwnd = 64 KB and RTT = 80 ms. What is the approximate maximum throughput?
options: 3.28 Mbps
5.12 Mbps
6.55 Mbps
8.00 Mbps

questions.question: A TCP sender starts with cwnd = 1 MSS and ssthresh = 32 MSS. How many RTTs are required for cwnd to reach ssthresh during slow start?
options: 3 RTTs
4 RTTs
5 RTTs
6 RTTs

questions.question: A TCP connection has cwnd = 24 MSS. A timeout occurs. What are the new cwnd and ssthresh?
options: cwnd = 12 MSS, ssthresh = 12 MSS
cwnd = 1 MSS, ssthresh = 24 MSS
cwnd = 1 MSS, ssthresh = 12 MSS
cwnd = 6 MSS, ssthresh = 12 MSS

questions.question: A TCP connection has cwnd = 30 MSS and a triple duplicate ACK occurs. What are the new cwnd and ssthresh after fast recovery?
options: cwnd = 1 MSS, ssthresh = 15 MSS
cwnd = 15 MSS, ssthresh = 15 MSS
cwnd = 15 MSS, ssthresh = 30 MSS
cwnd = 30 MSS, ssthresh = 15 MSS

questions.question: A link has bandwidth = 100 Mbps and RTT = 50 ms. What is the bandwidth-delay product (required window size)?
options: 500 KB
610 KB
625 KB
1 MB

questions.question: In TCP, reliability is achieved using byte numbering through sequence numbers, confirmation using acknowledgments, and recovery using:
options: Checksums
Retransmissions
Forward error correction
Selective repeat ARQ at the IP layer

questions.question: During TCP connection setup, the client sends a SYN, the server replies with SYN-ACK, and the client completes the handshake by sending:
options: SYN
FIN
ACK
RST

questions.question: In TCP congestion control, the initial exponential growth phase is called:
options: Congestion avoidance
Fast recovery
Slow start
Window scaling

questions.question: During TCP congestion avoidance, cwnd increases:
options: Exponentially, doubling once per RTT
Linearly (by 1 MSS per RTT)
By the square root of the current cwnd each RTT
In proportion to the available receiver buffer space

questions.question: When packet loss is detected via triple duplicate ACKs, TCP Reno sets ssthresh to what value?
options: 1 MSS
The current cwnd value
Half of the current cwnd
The initial ssthresh value from connection setup

questions.question: Why is fast recovery preferable to timeout-based recovery in TCP?
options: Fast recovery uses selective acknowledgments to repair gaps without retransmitting
Fast recovery avoids resetting cwnd to 1 MSS, maintaining higher throughput
Fast recovery skips the retransmission and relies on the receiver to reconstruct the segment
Fast recovery signals the router to prioritize the retransmitted packet in the queue

questions.question: Why is TCP window scaling necessary in high-speed networks?
options: IPv6 requires a larger window field to accommodate extended addressing overhead
The default 16-bit window size is too small for the bandwidth-delay product of high-speed links
Window scaling synchronizes sender and receiver clocks to reduce RTT measurement error
It enables the OS to allocate separate socket buffers for each TCP flow

questions.question: Two TCP flows share a link with RTTs of 20 ms and 200 ms. Which flow receives more bandwidth under standard TCP Reno?
options: The flow with RTT = 200 ms, because it probes the network less aggressively
Both flows receive equal bandwidth because TCP is designed to be fair
The flow with RTT = 20 ms
The flow that has been active longer, since it has a higher ssthresh

questions.question: A TCP flow over a 10 Gbps link with RTT = 100 ms achieves only 200 Mbps. What is the primary limitation?
options: Receiver-side buffer overflow causing frequent window-zero advertisements
Insufficient congestion window size
TCP checksum overhead saturating the CPU on the sender
ACK compression collapsing the feedback loop and delaying cwnd growth

questions.question: TCP exits slow start when:
options: A triple duplicate ACK is received
RTT increases by more than a configurable threshold
cwnd reaches ssthresh
The receiver window reaches its advertised maximum

questions.question: A receiver advertises a zero window and later frees buffer space, but the connection remains stalled. What is the most likely cause?
options: The sender's congestion window was reset to 1 MSS during the stall period
The receiver's TCP stack closed the connection after the zero-window timeout
The window update packet was lost and the persist timer failed
A routing change caused asymmetric paths, preventing ACKs from reaching the sender

questions.question: In IP fragmentation, a 4,000-byte IP packet (including 20-byte header) is sent over a link with MTU = 1,020 bytes. How many fragments are created?
Which of the following most accurately describes the difference between distance vector and link-state routing?
options: Distance vector uses Dijkstra's algorithm; link-state uses the Bellman-Ford equation
Distance vector routers share their full topology database; link-state routers share only neighbor costs
Distance vector can suffer from count-to-infinity; link-state avoids this with complete topology knowledge
Link-state is better suited to small stub networks; distance vector scales to large transit networks

questions.question: A TCP sender is in congestion avoidance with cwnd = 20 MSS. After 5 RTTs with no loss, what is cwnd?
options: 20 MSS
23 MSS
25 MSS
40 MSS

questions.question: Which field in an IP packet is decremented by each router and causes the packet to be discarded when it reaches zero?
options: Identification
Protocol
TTL (Time to Live)
Flags

questions.question: During DHCP lease renewal (at the T1 timer), the client sends its renewal request to:
options: The subnet broadcast address so any available DHCP server can respond
The original DHCP server via unicast
All DHCP servers via the 224.0.0.1 multicast group
The default gateway, which proxies the request to the DHCP server

questions.question: Why is subnetting used in IP networking?
options: To increase the total number of available IP addresses beyond the class-based limit
To extend the physical reach of a network segment beyond standard cable lengths
To organize networks and reduce broadcast domain size
To remove the need for inter-VLAN routing within a campus network

questions.question: Traceroute works because:
options: It queries the SNMP MIB of each intermediate router for its interface addresses
Routers send ICMP Time Exceeded messages when TTL expires in transit
Each router recognizes the traceroute probe port and sends its address in the reply
The source sets the record-route IP option, causing routers to insert their addresses
